OpenAI Introduces Virtual Try-On and Favorites for ChatGPT Shopping

OpenAI has globally launched new shopping features for its conversational AI assistant, ChatGPT, on Thursday. These updates aim to enhance online retail experiences by allowing users to virtually try on clothing and accessories and save desired products for later.

The new functionalities leverage the ChatGPT Images 2.5 model, which OpenAI states offers more natural lighting, richer textures, reliable editing instructions, and reduced image generation latency. Users can upload a selfie or full-body photo to visualize items, or even upload an image of an item to have ChatGPT try it on for them. A new “try on” button appears in shopping results to facilitate this.

Alongside the virtual try-on, a new Favorites option enables users to save discovered products to a Library within the app, storing them with try-on images. These developments position ChatGPT in areas previously dominated by platforms like Pinterest and Google, which launched its own virtual try-on feature last year.

OpenAI's move follows earlier experimentation in the shopping space, including an instant checkout feature that did not perform well. The company is now focusing on consumer use cases that integrate its advanced AI image generation with practical shopping tools.

TECH · Engadget · editor 9/10 · 1 min read fact-checked

Why you should avoid holding down your PC's power button

Most computer users have encountered a situation where their PC freezes, becoming unresponsive and requiring a hard shutdown. In such moments, the immediate instinct is often to press and hold the power button until the machine powers off. While this method can resolve an immediate hang, regularly resorting to it can introduce a range of potential issues for your computer's health and data integrity.

A hard shutdown forces the system to cut power abruptly, rather than going through its proper shutdown sequence. During a normal shutdown, the operating system closes all running applications, saves open files, and parks the hard drive heads safely before powering down. When you hold the power button, these critical steps are bypassed.

Repeated hard shutdowns can lead to file system corruption, which might result in lost data or even prevent the operating system from booting correctly. Furthermore, it can place undue stress on hardware components, particularly mechanical hard drives, potentially shortening their lifespan. While occasional use during an emergency is sometimes unavoidable, making it a regular practice increases the risk of system instability and hardware damage. It is always preferable to attempt a software-based shutdown or restart if possible, even if it requires patience.

What to watch: Prioritize proper shutdown procedures to safeguard your PC's longevity and data.
